summary: The early life of Joseph Stalin in Gori and Tiflis, Georgia, from his 1878 birth through parental beatings, street fights, Russified schooling and seminary radicalisation to his 1899 expulsion as a young Marxist.

evidence.note: host frames the episode as Stalin's childhood only
birth in Gori in 1878 opens the story
drunken father hurls the boy to the ground and hunts him at home
father beats the mother; she later beats the son harshly
Georgian banned in schools; harsh punishments, threat against teacher
gifted singer, painter and actor; works as a wedding singer
organises a near-riot protest against a school inspector
Darwin leads him to atheism; enters the Tiflis seminary
publishes acclaimed poetry as a teenager under a pen name
turns to Marxism and forms a more militant study circle
expelled from the seminary in May 1899
host closes the story at the threshold of adulthood

notes: partial_life set: title and host frame it as the childhood only, ending at the 1899 expulsion; adult rule gets passing asides, so covered_span is 1878-1899. Keke's birth follows the transcript (17 at her 1872 marriage); common sources give 1856 or 1858. Primary theme chosen for catalogue fit since the episode is framed as the making of a communist dictator; child-abuse is the close runner-up.
